cases.description: NewWithEvict(0,nil) returns a non-nil Cache pointer and a non-nil error; callers cannot treat that result as a successfully initialized cache.
With capacity two, Peek of the oldest key leaves it oldest while Get makes that key most recent; the next Add evicts the respective oldest key and reports the callback.
Purge invokes eviction callbacks outside the cache lock; a callback may reenter Add and leave a newly added entry after Purge returns.
With capacity two and one entry, Resize(-1) returns two while one existing entry is actually evicted; it leaves capacity -1 and a later Add immediately evicts its inserted entry.
Concurrent Cache.Cap and Cache.Resize access the underlying size without a common lock, producing a race-detector report on the size read and write.

open_questions.question: What behavior should Resize have for a negative capacity and what does its returned count mean?
What should Purge guarantee at return if an eviction callback reenters and adds an entry?
